multiplechoiceresponse.p: An employee moves from Finance to Marketing. The correct sequence is:

choice.div: Remove the Finance access, then grant the Marketing role's access.
Grant Marketing access and leave Finance access in place.
Create a brand-new account and abandon the old one.

div.p: A mover should end with exactly the new role's access. Leaving the old access creates privilege creep.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Role-based access control (RBAC) means access is granted to:

choice.div: Roles, and users are placed in those roles.
Whichever account is fastest to set up.

div.p: Roles make access auditable and consistent, and removal as simple as changing a group.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which is the strongest control for an administrator account?

choice.div: A separate admin identity with MFA and just-in-time elevation.
A long password shared with the team.
Making the admin a local account with no MFA.

div.p: Separate identities plus MFA plus time-limited elevation limit both the chance and the blast radius of a compromised admin account. Shared passwords destroy accountability.
